title: Photographer

fields.label: Where you're based
fields.help: Town or city, and how far you travel.

fields.label: What you shoot
fields.help: Portraits, weddings, families, brands, products, events. Your look: warm, black and white, cool and clean.

fields.label: Packages and prices
fields.help: For each kind of shoot: package names, prices, time, how many photos and what's included.

fields.label: How a booking goes
fields.help: From first call to gallery: what happens and when, and how fast photos are delivered.

fields.label: Availability
fields.help: How far ahead people need to book, and days you don't shoot.

fields.label: Brand colour
fields.help: Optional: one colour for buttons and highlights.

writerNotes: The hero lights one frame in the studio, light by light: the backdrop in the dark, the key light, fill, rim light, background light, then the shot and the finished print, beside a lighting diagram. shot.subject: portrait for portrait, wedding, family or brand photographers; product for product photographers (then product.name and product.line are what the bottle's label says, from the brief or a plausible product of theirs). shot.look: warm, mono if the brief's style is black and white, cool for clean commercial work.
shot settings are plausible for the subject (portrait f/2.8 1/200; product f/8 1/125); ratio like 3:1; frames and keepers for a typical shoot; the caption names the frame and place.
Write the six stages for that subject, keeping the order (backdrop, key, fill, rim, background, the frame).

sessions.kinds: the brief's kinds of shoot (one to four), each with one to three packages exactly as priced in the brief: name, price, time, photos delivered, up to five inclusions and an optional short tag on the one most booked. Use from: true only when the brief says 'from'. sessions.start picks the kind and package shown first.
process: the brief's steps from enquiry to gallery with when each happens; delivers: up to three short numbers that matter (48 h, 2 weeks). Never promise delivery times the brief doesn't give.

book.lead: how far ahead a date can be held, in days; book.closed: days the photographer never shoots. The calendar sends a real request: the photographer replies to confirm and hold the date. Never say a date is held or booked.

hero.title and hero.titleEm: a short two-part headline (four lines at most on a desktop); the section titles have an italic second half (titleEm). theme.accent is one strong colour, deep enough for white button text; theme.wordmarkFit is always "fit".
business.name is set to exactly the name in the brief and cannot be changed; brand.name is how it appears in the nav and the footer (short).
